title: The Hindenburg Disaster
caption:
97 people were seconds from landing. Then an 804-foot airship burst into flames. 🔥

A radio reporter was recording the whole time, and his words became famous.

Tragic accident, or something more? Tell us below 👇

scenes.say: A giant airship landing in New Jersey burst into flames. 7:25 PM, May 6, 1937. 804 feet long, gone in under a minute.
The Hindenburg. 97 people aboard, three days out from Frankfurt, Germany.
Thunderstorms had delayed the landing for hours. The captain circled the Jersey shore, waiting for clear skies.
Its giant gas cells were filled with hydrogen. One spark, and it burns.
On the ground, radio reporter Herbert Morrison was recording. Then he shouted, 'It burst into flames!'
Fire raced along the ship. In just over 30 seconds, it crashed to the ground.
Morrison kept recording, his voice breaking. 'Oh, the humanity, and all the passengers screaming around here!'
Passengers jumped from the windows as it fell. Incredibly, 62 people survived. 36 died.
The likely cause? A static spark igniting leaking hydrogen. Sabotage was never proven.
The disaster ended the age of passenger airships almost overnight. And the whole thing was caught on film.
Was it an accident, or something more? Tell me in the comments.

shots.action: The giant silver airship glides slowly through the evening sky, its shadow sliding across the clouds below
Passengers at the airship's windows gaze down at the coastline as the airship drifts slowly forward
Storm clouds roll across the sky and lightning flashes while the airship circles slowly in the distance
The huge gas cells inside the airship sway gently, light flickers across the metal girders of the frame
The radio reporter speaks urgently into his microphone while the crowd behind him looks up at the sky
Flames race along the airship from tail to nose, thick black smoke billows into the night sky
The reporter grips the microphone and turns his face away in shock, the fire glowing behind him
The burning airship sinks slowly toward the field, ground crew run away across the grass
Ground crew run toward the wreck through drifting smoke, flames still flickering in the metal frame
A tiny spark flickers near the airship's tail, then a small flame bursts into life and spreads
The charred metal skeleton of the airship smokes on the field as the camera slowly pulls back
Smoke drifts slowly across the burned wreckage under a dark, cloudy sky
